newsitem.title: BENIN: "Child slave" traffickers arrested in Benin.
newsitem.headline: "Child slave" traffickers arrested in Benin.

text.p: Police in Benin say they have arrested five West Africans on suspicion of trafficking in "child slaves" -- minors bought from their families with promises of lucrative work abroad.

Police commissioner Max Aweke in the capital Porto Novo told Reuters the five -- two from Benin, two from Togo and one from Niger -- were caught red-handed as they prepared to ship 90 minors from Benin to Gabon. Some were as young as eight.
He said late on Thursday the five would be charged under a 36-year-old law to punish such traffic.
Police say that they have intercepted 702 minors at the borders in the first six months of 1997 against just 413 for the whole of 1996.

A report from the juvenile protection brigade says Benin has been a source of cheap, illegal child labour for richer countries in West and Central Africa such as Ivory Coast, Gabon Congo, Cameroon, Nigeria and Equatorial Guinea since 1987.
The report highlights cases of abuse and exploitation, saying six children died in service in the first half of 1997 while others were raped, beaten or forced into prostitution.

Police say the latest consignment of children was recruited in the north of neighbouring Togo and in south Benin with the traffickers paying 20,000 CFA francs ($34) per child to the families and promising good jobs abroad.
The existing law carries a jail sentence of only three to six months. Police say parliament is studying a new law.
